quote: In relative terms, StoneDB's bulk-insert throughput was about 54 percent higher than KVLite's.
problem: A2 gives 348 vs 212 thousand ops/s, which is about 64 percent higher (348/212 = 1.64), not 54 percent.

quote: Under the mixed workload, KVLite's median p99 latency was 4.2 ms, the worst of the three, against 3.1 ms for StoneDB and 2.9 ms for Marlin.
problem: A3 gives the KVLite p99 median as 4.8 ms [4.5-5.2], not 4.2 ms.

quote: Marlin's higher write throughput comes from its batched write-ahead log, which groups concurrent writes into a single append.
problem: Causal attribution is unsupported. A1 says no profiler, tracing or ablation runs were collected for any store, and A7 is only a README design statement, not a measurement.

quote: Marlin's write advantage holds regardless of storage hardware or durability settings.
problem: A1 shows one machine with one NVMe SSD, a fixed batched-fsync setting for all stores, and states per-write fsync was not tested, so this generality is not supported.

quote: StoneDB sustains its mixed-workload throughput over long-running operation.
problem: A1 says the longest single run was 6 minutes including warm-up and that no soak or multi-hour run was performed. A5 covers only five minutes of one run.

quote: As for what the projects say about themselves, Marlin's own documentation presents it as the right engine for write-intensive systems generally.
problem: A7 quotes the README as designed for write-intensive workloads whose reads mostly touch recently written keys. The body drops that restriction and overgeneralizes.

quote: Wray kept a continuous day-by-day record of the winter.
problem: E1 records no entries from 12 December 1741 to 26 January 1742 (a 46-day gap) and missing folios 31-34, so the record is not continuous.

quote: The parish register shows 52 burials in 1742, which is 23 more than in 1741.
problem: E5(a) gives 33 burials in 1741. 52 minus 33 is 19, not 23.

quote: Of the 29 death entries in the journal, Wray names a fever as the cause in seven.
problem: E5(b) says fever is named in 5 death entries (cold or frost in 6), not 7.

quote: The frost alone accounts for the rise in burials in 1742.
problem: Unsupported causal claim. E5(b) names frost in only 6 of 29 entries and gives no cause for 18; the appendix contains no analysis that isolates frost.

quote: Wray's burial entries have been checked against the parish register and found accurate.
problem: Q8 says only nine of Wray's burial notices were compared with the register, and that the remainder were not checked. The body generalizes to all entries.

quote: Wray states that the vicar kept the tithe barn locked against the poor.
problem: Q5 is hearsay ('It is said by some'), and Wray adds that he has not seen it with his own eyes. He does not state it as fact.

quote: The journal gives a representative picture of how rural parishes in the county fared that winter.
problem: E1 says the edition covers one parish and prints no records or comparative material from any other parish, so representativeness cannot be established.

quote: Of the 48 nurses who were screened but not randomized, most (31) declined to take part.
problem: T2 gives 31 of the 48 as ineligible and 17 as declined. Only 17 declined.

quote: Across both arms, 56 of 64 participants (85.9%) completed the week 8 assessment.
problem: 56 of 64 is 87.5%, as T2 states. 85.9% is wrong.

quote: The reduction in insomnia severity persisted after the program ended.
problem: T1 says assessments were only at baseline and week 8, and T7 section 6.3 says no follow-up after week 8 is planned, so persistence was not measured.

quote: The sleep-restriction module is what drove the improvement.
problem: T7 section 3.1 says components are delivered together and the study does not test individual components, so no module-level attribution is supported.

quote: Engagement with the program was high.
problem: T5 shows a median of 5 of 8 modules, only 11 of 32 (34.4%) completing all eight, and 8 completing three or fewer. The appendix does not support calling engagement high.

quote: These data show the program is safe for night-shift nurses.
problem: T7 section 7.4 says the study is not powered to estimate adverse event rates. The data are 32 per arm, self-reported, with two mild events in the app arm, which cannot show safety.

quote: The findings apply to shift workers generally.
problem: All participants were nurses at one teaching hospital (body and T1), so generalization to shift workers in general is not supported.

quote: Below 3.0 kN the bracket has an effectively infinite fatigue life.
problem: F3 states no specimen was tested below 3.0 kN, so this is an extrapolation with no supporting data.

quote: One of the four specimens reached the runout and the other three failed, the shortest at 1,138,000 cycles.
problem: F3 and F5 give the shortest 4.0 kN failure as F4-04 at 1,238,000 cycles, not 1,138,000.

quote: At 4.0 kN the bracket has a 75 percent chance of failing before two million cycles.
problem: This is 3 of 4 observed failures, not an estimated probability. F2 says no statistical analysis of the fatigue data was performed, and n=4 cannot support a failure probability.

quote: The mean life at 5.0 kN was about 483,000 cycles.
The excess set in S08 is explained by its coming from a different material lot.
problem: Causal claim unsupported. F2 says the lot B mill certificate was not on file, and F5 says no sectioning, hardness or tensile tests on lot B were scheduled.

quote: The bracket's performance carries over to the full range of service temperatures.
problem: All tests were at 20.1-22.6 C and F2 says no tests were run at other temperatures, while REQ-EN-003 in F1 requires operation from -30 C to +50 C.

quote: The fatigue programme was run in accordance with ASTM E466.
problem: F1 says the method was 'adapted from' ASTM E466 with listed deviations. Section 4 records four specimens per level against a plan target of six, and frame alignment was not verified.
